Truth and reason are good ideas worth defending and striving towards. If you are seeker of Truth and reason, and if you think this pursuit is just, then you have a moral obligation to use the tools of nature at your disposal in order to get there. The reality is that the realm of human nature and politics is not a realm of pure rationalism. If you have spent anytime analyzing the current political arena and looking back at the past with hindsight, you know this to be unarguably true. This is true even in yourself. Where you see objectivity and Truth, an outsider may see partisanship, personal bias, selfishness, and relative morality. You try to appeal towards a political opponent using facts and evidence, but it never seems to work - why? Because, it is irrational to assume that it would.

The reality is, that even the most objective and scientific of people see the world through a biased lens based on personal values. A three minute commercial of a woman and her daughter trying to pursue a better life, can undermine all the facts and evidence of the terrible outcomes of an open border policy. This is known as 'the narrative.'

I am not proposing that you throw out your facts and evidence in favor of pure irrationality, but that you use romanticism to highlight the real. You are still fighting over facts and reality, but you must appeal to humanity, nature, sentimentality, and emotion, in order to win the debate. You do not win an argument against a three minute commercial that highlights the innocence of particular illegal immigrants, with facts about illegal immigration crime rates, national sovereignty, jobs, etc. You highlight these facts and values with a counter appeal of romanticism, by showing the stories of the innocent mothers who lose their sons to illegal immigrant crime. You highlight the hard working family man who can't get a job in the cutthroat economy. You highlight the nation that is losing it's identity and values to people who do not share our ideals. You highlight all these truths by showing them in the light of romantic narratives and stories.

I am also not insinuating that the end justifies the means, and that you should use lies to shift the narrative. This is propaganda. This is how you lose the culture war. You have to battle their romanticism with your romanticism, based on virtue and truth. If you rely completely on reason, you will lose. If you rely on messages that are hollow, you will lose. Make your romantic appeal so that they can only argue against it based on a differences of values. Then it becomes a debate for what is good and what is bad. If your side is on the side of truth and reason, you will win. It's hard to argue that a burnt out drug user who has gone through the cock carousel, has a more fulfilling life than a women who marries a loving and supporting husband, who gives her stability and a family whom to love and to love her back. This is how you argue against some who is a SJW-lite, not with facts. (Notice how I don't say that you can really change the minds of an SJW. You really can't, when you argue against them you are appealing to the observer, not the person on the other side of the debate.)

Keep seeking truth and reason. But, do so by shining a positive light on those things in life that are good, virtuous, and true, and shining a negative light on those things in life that are bad, wicked, and false.
